notes.decision: Translated as interrogative 'what.' Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲉⲩ/ⲁϣ 'what.' The full phrase ⲉⲱ ⲧⲉ ⲧⲍⲉ = 'what is the manner' opens Mani's exposition as a rhetorical-interrogative declaration about the Sun's fashioning. Standard Kephalaia opening pattern.

Translated 'stronghold' rather than 'dwelling-place.' The form ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲣⲉ with -ⲣⲉ ending matches the glossary entry ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ 'stronghold/fortress' (ⲙⲁⲛ-ϫⲱⲣⲉ 'place of strength') rather than ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲡⲉ 'dwelling.' The pairing 'gate of Life and stronghold of Peace' fits the Manichaean cosmographic image of the Sun as both threshold (gate) and fortified citadel of Peace.

The ⲭ̄ⲉ markers (with supralinear stroke) are decorative chapter-abbreviation symbols (= κεφάλαιον), used to bracket the new chapter title at line 25. Rendered as '§' to preserve the structural-divisional function without inventing English text.

Translated 'gate of the going-forth of the souls.' ⲡⲣⲟ here = ⲣⲟ 'mouth, door, gate' (with article). ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the Lyc. action-noun on ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'come forth, go out' (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ in glossary). Satan is identified as the threshold through which souls must pass at exit — hence his motivation to set up legal barriers against the Light.

Translated 'the Light who shall slay him.' ⲟⲩⲱⲥϥ̄ = ⲟⲩⲱϣϥ 'shatter, smite, slay' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲡϥ context). The clause continues Satan's quoted edict: he calls the Light by this destructive epithet to inspire fear among the souls.

Translated 'commanded them.' Likely Lyc. form on ⲟⲩⲉϩ-ⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command' or ⲟⲩⲱϩⲉ 'set, place,' with 3pl object suffix. Combined with the following ⲁϩⲧⲣⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲡⲁⲣⲛⲉ 'to make them deny' the verb governs a compulsion-clause.

Translated 'manner' (= ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion'). The Lyc. ⲍⲙⲁⲧ corresponds to Sah. ⲥⲙⲟⲧ; here parallel with line 15 ⲛⲉϩⲍⲙⲁⲧ 'his manners/ways.' Distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' (mandatory consistent translation reserved). 'Manner' captures the fashion/way in which the Light shines.
Translated 'mercies.' Likely Lyc. form for ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲁⲏⲧ/ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁ 'mercy, compassion' (cf. accumulated ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ 'mercies'). The plural in line 14 (ⲛⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ 'loves') confirms a positive-affective register.

Translated 'he does seven good things.' ϣⲁϩ- is the Lyc. habitual prefix (= Sah. ϣⲁϥ-) recurring throughout this passage (lines 16, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25-26, 27, 30). ⲥⲁϣϩ = ⲥⲁϣϥ 'seven.' This introduces the structural enumeration of seven goods, of which only the first three survive on this page.

Translated 'while he bears away from them.' Reading ϩ̄ⲃⲓ as the same habitual ϣⲁϩ-ⲃⲓ pattern attested in line 24 ϣⲁϩⲃⲓ ⲍⲱⲱϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'he himself takes away from them.' ⲃⲓ = 'carry, bear, take away.' The line 26 [ⲃ{ⲓ}] ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ confirms the pattern: 'he bears the darkness.'

Translated 'draws (them) out.' Reduplicated form on ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Habitual ϣⲁϩ- = 'he habitually draws/lifts forth.' The clause forms a typological mirror to lines 24-26 (he bears away fear and darkness).

Translated 'the wakeful ones ... cease their hand.' ⲛⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ϣⲉ = 'those of vigil/wakefulness' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲱⲉ 'the Watchers'). ⲕⲁ ⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = standard Coptic idiom 'leave/cease one's hand from = stop doing.' The night-watchers stand down because the Illuminator's vigilance has replaced theirs.
Translated 'in fear.' ⲍⲟⲩⲣⲉⲧⲉ = Lyc. reflex of ϩⲟⲣⲟⲧⲉ/ϩⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (cf. ⲑⲣ̄ⲧⲉ in line 24 — same root). The ⲛ̄- is genitive: 'watch of fear' = 'fearful watch.'

Translated as 'gives taste and scent.' ⲧⲡⲉ taken as 'taste/savor' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲡⲧⲉ 'the taste') paired with ⲥⲧⲁⲓ̈ 'scent' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲉⲥⲧⲉ 'scent') — the sensory-correspondence pair characteristic of the Manichaean register. The double-dagger †† before ⲡⲉ is unusual; likely a transcription artifact for ϯ-ⲧⲡⲉ 'give-taste.' Confidence moderate.

Rendered 'the crops.' †ⲟⲉ likely = ϯⲟⲉ, a vegetative/agricultural noun (cf. ⲟⲉⲓⲕ 'bread, grain' or related growth term) appearing between ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits' and ⲗⲁⲭⲁⲛⲟⲛ 'vegetables.' Etymology uncertain.

Translated 'the evil creeping things and the predatory wild beasts.' ⲡⲝⲉⲧϩⲉ confirmed in glossary (= ϫⲁⲧϥⲉ 'creeping thing/reptile'). ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲗⲟⲁⲃϩⲉ unclear — rendered 'predatory' on the reading of a root for rapacious/devouring beasts. Confidence low.

Translated 'the lair, into their dens.' ⲕⲱⲡ taken as 'hidden place, lair' (cf. ϩⲱⲡ 'be hidden'); ⲃⲏⲃ Sahidic 'hole, den.' Both fit zoological-cosmological register: at sunrise the harmful animals withdraw to concealment.

Rendered 'is at rest from the affliction.' ⲡⲧⲕⲉⲥ taken as = Sah. ⲧⲱⲕⲥ 'stab, sting, affliction' (Crum). The plague of men finds relief from the stinging pain at sunrise. The idiom ⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ ϩⲁ 'rest under/from' = 'be relieved from.'

Translated 'is poured forth — dissolving — from.' Greek-derived ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄/ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ has the dual sense 'pour forth' and 'wipe out, dissolve' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'dissolution'). Both senses operate here: light is poured out and thereby dissolves the evil magics.

Tentatively rendered 'vain-show.' Compound ⲙⲛⲧ- (abstract) + ⲃⲁⲛ-ϣⲁⲓ̈ — etymology uncertain. Context: the rival doctrine is exposed as a 'X' set up by the Errant teacher. The semantic field is that of futility/pretense/empty-display — the sun's revelation shows up the rival doctrine as hollow appearance. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Translated 'the other nourishings (services).' ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ = abstract from ⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ 'food, nourishment' (in glossary) = 'state of nourishing, providing.' The sun's nourishing functions paralleled to its other revelatory acts.

Rendered 'he is the doer.' Likely ⲡⲉ + ϯⲣⲉ (ⲡⲉⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲉ) 'he is the doer/giver' — the sun is identified as the active agent producing the seven goods. The dagger-form preserves the ϯ- ('give/do') element in the participial-agentive expression.

Translated 'with itself.' Reflexive: the night fills the cosmos with itself = with its own substance/quality, the Darkness IS what fills. Direct correspondence-register: the night's act of filling and her own being are one.

The ordinals are written with doubled article ⲧⲧ-, marking the feminine ordinal series throughout. Translated as 'The first / The second / The third...' enumerating five attributes of the Father followed by three further 'types' revealed in the sun. The doubled-article form is a Lycopolitan dialectal feature already attested in this corpus.
Translated as 'his light, because he gives-light through his light': ϥ̄ⲧⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ is causative ⲧⲣⲉ-ⲣ̄-ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'cause to give light' = 'illuminate'; ⲍⲏ̄ taken as instrumental 'through.'

Parsed ϣⲁϩ as the Lycopolitan habitual prefix (= Sah. ϣⲁϥ-) on verb ϣⲱⲗ. The verb ϣⲱⲗ is rendered 'pour forth / spread out / shed' from context (the sun habitually distributing beauty and uprightness over creation). Crum lists ϣⲱⲗ as a verb of distributive action; semantic precision low.
Lycopolitan ⲍ for ⲥ: ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟⲩⲧⲱⲛ 'uprightness, rectitude, straightness.' The pairing with 'beauty' suggests aesthetic-moral order — the regular, upright structure that the sun's light reveals.

The feminine relative ⲧⲉⲧⲉ + habitual ϣⲁϩ-ⲃⲁⲗ-ⲥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ takes 3sg.f object referring back to ⲧϯⲩⲭⲏ 'the soul.' Translated 'whom he habitually releases out from her' — recasting in idiomatic English as 'whom he habitually releases out of all the fruits.' Using 'release' per glossary terminology rule for ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ.

The form ϩϯ (and its parallel ⲛ̄ϩ̄ϯ ⲁⲛ) appears to function as a finite verbal form 'he gives' — possibly a Lycopolitan/scribal contraction of ϣⲁϥϯ (habitual) or ⲁϥϯ (perfect). The ϩ may be a graphic variant for ϥ. Translated as present 'he gives.'

The Cross of Light (σταυρὸς τοῦ φωτός) — the Manichaean cosmic figure of dispersed light suffering in matter (the Jesus patibilis), the totality of light-particles bound throughout creation. Receiving 'scent and taste' is consistent with the correspondential register of this kephalaion: each cosmic register IS a sensory mode.

Lexeme of uncertain analysis. Possibly Lyc. ⲛⲁ-ⲟⲩⲣⲡⲉ-ϣⲉ 'those of the (sent ones / dignitaries / officers)' from ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ 'send,' yielding 'envoys/embassies/officials.' Translated 'rulers' in parallel with the immediately preceding ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' — the doublet 'powers and rulers' as cosmic authorities. Confidence low; flagged in apparatus as restoration with proposed reading.

Literally 'she is a great one of days.' Translated 'is great in days' — i.e., great in temporal extent / abundance. The phrase may also evoke the Manichaean cosmological 'Great Days' (ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲟⲩⲉ in glossary), but here functions as the comparative measure of the Father's release-act over against all other dissolutions.

Comparative correspondential clause: 'in the same manner that the disc of the moon does not diminish.' The moon's full disc, even when it appears to wax and wane, retains its true fullness — typological proof of the Father's invariant fullness despite emanating powers and gods.

Reading per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ: 'not to consent / not be like.' Here in the construction 'deficiency does not come to be in him X' — translated 'at all,' taking ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ as an adverbial intensifier of the negation. Could alternatively read 'without measure' (privative ⲁⲧ- + ⲙⲉⲧ-).

Translated 'the third' (feminine ordinal). The doubled ⲧⲧ- represents article + ordinal-prefix. The implied feminine antecedent (saying / sign / mystery) is ambiguous; left bare 'the third' to preserve the enumerative force without unwarranted specification.

Rendered 'raised' preserving the verbal-directional sense of ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (per terminology guide). Here functioning as verbal noun parallel to qualitative ⲭⲁⲥⲉ 'is exalted/high' — a doublet of elevation-vocabulary. Vertical semantics retained, not flattened.

Rendered 'is hidden.' The element ⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲉ likely relates to ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲧⲉ 'hidden chamber/repository' (accumulated vocabulary), here functioning verbally with subject prefix ϥ̄- 'he.' Possible analysis: ⲙⲁ-ⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲉ ('place-of-hiding') with predicative use, yielding 'he is in (a) hidden state.' Same root as ⲍⲏⲡ 'hidden' (line 21, 26).

Rendered 'of heaven. As visions, behold them...' — parsing ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ as 'of heaven' (Sah. ⲡⲉ 'heaven, sky') governed by ⲡⲥⲱⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'creation,' giving 'creation of heaven.' ⲛ̄ⲁⲟⲣⲙⲁ then begins a new clause: '(as) visions, behold them in their wandering.' Alternative reading 'the two visions' (treating ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ as scribal abbreviation for ⲡⲓⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ) is possible but less natural.

Greek loanwords ἄταφος 'unburied' in three forms: indefinite (ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ), definite neuter (ⲡⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲛ), and adjectival (ⲛⲁⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ). The cosmological doctrine: the Sun is 'unburied' — i.e., not subjected to dissolution/decay, sharing this quality of substance with the unburied Father. Direct correspondence between Sun and Father preserved in the three-fold repetition.

Translated 'shadow.' Feminine form of ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' (cf. ⲍⲁⲃⲉⲥ in glossary, masculine form). Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ. The night-as-shadow stands in correspondence with the cosmic darkness-mystery, paralleling sun-as-light corresponding to Father-mystery.
ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ = ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' + ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ from ϫⲱⲣⲙ 'wink, signal.' Idiom: 'cast a sign, give a winking signal.' The Savior gives a hidden indication to the disciples about the hidden mystery.

Read as functioning negation marker ('not'), yielding 'You are NOT sons of the night and sons of the darkness.' This matches the Pauline source (1 Thess 5:5) which the apostle is quoting. ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ may be a Lycopolitan variant or scribal form of the negative ⲁⲛ; alternative parsings (relative perfect 'who became,' or as connective 'of those of') do not yield the expected biblical sense. The doctrinal context (children of light vs. darkness) and the ⲡⲁⲭⲉ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ 'said the apostle' framing make the Pauline citation certain.

Both forms construed as Lycopolitan present-I declarative formulas of teacher-disciple address: 'I am declaring/proclaiming (it/them) to you/to your souls.' The exact morphology is uncertain — ⲛⲉⲓⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ may = ⲛⲉⲓ̈- (pres I) + dat 2pl ⲧⲏⲛⲉ; ⲛⲉⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲟⲩ likely Pres I + 3pl object 'them.' Translated 'declare/proclaim' to fit the rhetorical context of revealing mysteries.

Read as Lycopolitan ⲛϥ-(ⲇⲓ)ⲁⲕⲣⲓⲛⲉ 'that he may discriminate/distinguish.' Greek loanword διακρίνειν, the technical verb for the dualist act of distinguishing the two substances of light and darkness. The doubled ⲁⲁ may reflect /διa-/ via vowel assimilation.
